turns.t: It's the swallowing, doctor. Solid food sticks in my chest, and I'm after having the stretching done, and it's still not right.
I see from the notes you had the dilatation. Tell me how it's been since.
Better for a week, then it came back. Bread and meat especially.
Where does it stick?
Just here, behind the breastbone.
When was the procedure, exactly?
Oh, about two months ago. Or six weeks. I'm not sure now.
Our record shows it was done on the twelfth, which would be nine weeks ago.
Thank you, Nurse. We'll go with the record, though Mr Walsh remembers it a bit differently. Any pain on swallowing?
No pain. It just stops. ~
Do liquids go down all right? ~
Yes. It's only solids. ~
Any weight loss, or vomiting food back up?
I've lost a bit of weight, maybe two kilos. No vomiting.
What medicines are you taking?
The omeprazole, 20 mg, twice a day.
The record shows once a day.
No, it's twice. The consultant said double it.
I'll note that you say twice, and the record says once, and we'll check with the pharmacy.
Any other conditions?
Reflux, for a good few years. That's why I had the stretching.
Doctor, I've got his observations. Pulse 76, blood pressure 128 over 80, temperature 36.6, oxygen 98 percent, weight 79 kilograms.
Thank you. Let me feel your neck and tummy. ~
Go on.
Neck is normal, and the abdomen is soft and non-tender.
What's going on, doctor? ~
The narrowing may be coming back, which can happen after a stretch. I'd like to repeat the camera test and see.
The endoscopy again?
Yes. I'll arrange it within the next two weeks, and we'll take a small sample at the same time.
That's fine. I'd rather know. ~
Until then, eat soft foods, cut meat into small pieces, and chew slowly.
I will. ~
If food gets completely stuck, you can't swallow your saliva, or you vomit blood, go straight to the emergency department.
Understood. Thank you both. ~
I'll see you after the endoscopy.
